context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries within an EU data residency boundary. It ensures high-performance patron search capabilities and robust administrative workflows.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Students, Public Citizens)
* Librarians / Library Staff
* Library Administrators
* Third-Party Vendors / Interlibrary Loan (ILL) Partners
* Library Management System (System-in-Scope)
* EU Identity Provider (Keycloak / EU Auth0)
* Digital Content Delivery Network / S3-compatible EU Object Storage
* SEPA / Stripe EU API Payment Gateway
* External Notification Service (EU Mailgun / Twilio)
* Centralized SIEM / Monitoring Platform (Datadog EU / Grafana Cloud Frankfurt)

## Relationships
* Library Patrons to Library Management System via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 for self-service portals
* Librarians and Administrators to Library Management System via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 for cataloging and management
* Library Management System to EU Identity Provider via OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0
* Library Management System to Digital Content Storage via HTTPS
* Library Management System to Payment Gateway via REST API over HTTPS
* Library Management System to ILL Partners via ISO ILL protocol or REST/JSON over HTTPS with mTLS
* Library Management System to Notification Service and SIEM via HTTPS/TLS 1.3

## Technology Stack
* OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 via Keycloak or EU Auth0: Ensures identity data remains strictly within EU boundaries
* S3-compatible EU-region Object Storage: Fulfills digital item cataloging and streaming requirements (R-01)
* SEPA / Stripe EU API: Handles regulated fines and fee processing
* HTTPS / TLS 1.3 with mTLS: Enforces secure transport across all external and internal integrations
* Datadog EU / Grafana Cloud Frankfurt: Provides centralized audit logging and telemetry within the EU

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees strict EU data residency compliance while isolating workloads to meet the p99 search response time under 800ms. External integrations utilize resilient protocols, circuit breakers, and asynchronous queuing to protect core library operations from third-party latency.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures strict EU data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons and Librarians/Administrators
- Web Application (SPA)
- API Gateway
- Core Services API (Modular Monolith)
- Search Engine
- Database
- Async Message Broker
- External Systems: EU Identity Provider, EU Object Storage, SEPA/Stripe EU API Payment Gateway, External Notification Service, SIEM

## Relationships
- Library Patrons/Librarians -> HTTPS -> Web Application (SPA)
- Web Application (SPA) -> HTTPS -> API Gateway
- API Gateway -> REST/gRPC -> Core Services API
- Core Services API -> TCP -> PostgreSQL & Search Engine
- Core Services API -> AMQP -> Async Message Broker

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript for Web Application (SPA)
- Node.js/NestJS for Core Services API
- Elasticsearch/OpenSearch for Search Engine
- PostgreSQL for transactional database
- RabbitMQ/Apache Kafka for Async Message Broker
- Nginx/Envoy for API Gateway
- Kubernetes (EKS/AKS) and Docker for orchestration

## Rationale
This architecture uses an isolated Search Engine and asynchronous messaging to guarantee sub-800ms search performance under load. Deploying all containers exclusively within managed EU cloud regions satisfies strict data residency mandates.

Web Application (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It ensures EU-only data residency and meets strict search performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- **Web Application (SPA)**: React / TypeScript frontend
- **Routing & Layout Manager**: React Router client-side routing
- **State Management Store**: Zustand or Redux Toolkit
- **API Client Layer**: Axios-configured HTTP client
- **Feature Modules**: Catalog Discovery, Circulation Desk, and Admin Dashboard components
- **Local Persistence Layer**: IndexedDB via Dexie.js with Web Crypto API encryption
- **API Gateway**: Nginx / Envoy
- **Core Services API**: Node.js / NestJS Modular Monolith

## Relationships
- **Library Patrons, Librarians, Administrators** -> **Web Application (SPA)**: Accesses portals and workflows [HTTPS]
- **Web Application (SPA)** -> **API Gateway**: Sends API requests [HTTPS / JSON]
- **Circulation Desk Component** -> **Local Persistence Layer**: Reads/writes cached transaction queues [IndexedDB]

## Technology Stack
- **React / TypeScript**: Chosen for building a modular, type-safe, and interactive single-page application.
- **IndexedDB & Dexie.js**: Enables robust local persistence for offline circulation resilience.
- **Web Crypto API**: Enforces client-side encryption-at-rest for PII to maintain GDPR compliance.
- **EU-hosted S3-compatible Object Storage**: Hosts static SPA assets to satisfy EU-only data residency constraints.

## Rationale
This architecture uses client-side caching, local persistence, and static asset distribution to achieve sub-800ms search responses and offline resilience for librarians. Furthermore, EU-hosted deployment and client-side encryption strictly enforce regional data residency and GDPR mandates.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The architecture enforces strict EU-only data residency and high-performance requirements.

## Key Elements
* API Gateway: Nginx / Envoy deployed on Kubernetes with Pod Disruption Budget
* Edge Components: Routing & Tenant Resolver, Rate Limiter Filter, Authentication/OAuth2 Proxy, Versioning & Transformation Filter
* Supporting Services: Redis Cache (in-memory rate limiting), EU Identity Provider, Core Services API (Node.js / NestJS), Centralized SIEM / Monitoring Platform

## Relationships
* Web Application (SPA) -> API Gateway: Sends API requests with JWT [HTTPS]
* API Gateway -> Core Services API: Forwards routed requests with W3C Trace Context [REST/gRPC]
* API Gateway -> Redis Cache: Queries rate limit counters [TCP/RESP]
* API Gateway -> Centralized SIEM / Monitoring Platform: Exports Prometheus metrics and access logs [HTTPS/Prometheus scrape]

## Technology Stack
* Nginx / Envoy: Perimeter routing, TLS 1.3 termination, and edge security for WAF protection
* Redis: Sliding-window rate limiting within the EU cluster to maintain data residency
* Kubernetes: Zero-downtime deployments, hot-reloads, and multi-zone resilience

## Rationale
The API Gateway centralizes security, tenant routing, rate limiting, and auth offloading at the perimeter to protect core services. This ensures compliance with EU data residency and supports high-performance self-service portals.

Core Services API.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides physical/digital cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals. It uses a containerized modular monolith deployed on Kubernetes, strictly enforcing EU data residency.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Library Patrons, Library Staff, Library Administrators
- **Core Services API**: Node.js / NestJS Modular Monolith
- **Internal Modules**: Catalog Module, Circulation Module, Fines & Fees Module, Search Orchestrator Module, Data Governance Interceptor
- **Data & Storage**: PostgreSQL (Database), Elasticsearch / OpenSearch (Search Engine), S3-compatible EU Object Storage
- **Infrastructure & Integration**: Nginx / Envoy (API Gateway), RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka (Async Message Broker), SEPA / Stripe EU API Payment Gateway, Centralized SIEM / Monitoring Platform

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Core Services API: Forwards routed requests [REST/gRPC]
- Core Services API -> PostgreSQL: Reads/writes transactional data [TCP]
- Core Services API -> OpenSearch: Queries/indexes search data [TCP]
- Core Services API -> RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka: Publishes/consumes async messages [AMQP]
- Core Services API -> SEPA / Stripe EU API Payment Gateway: Processes fines and fees [REST API over HTTPS]
- Core Services API -> Centralized SIEM / Monitoring Platform: Sends audit logs and telemetry [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- **Backend**: Node.js / NestJS for the modular monolith architecture
- **Database**: PostgreSQL with TypeORM for relational data storage
- **Search**: OpenSearch / Elasticsearch for low-latency search (<800ms SLA)
- **Deployment**: Kubernetes with containerized workloads and Istio/Envoy gateway
- **Observability**: OpenTelemetry for request tracing and structured JSON logging

## Rationale
The modular monolith structure supports rapid feature delivery while isolating high-churn domain logic. Containerizing on Kubernetes with strict EU data residency enforcement guarantees both high availability and regulatory compliance.

Search Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries within EU data residency constraints. The Search Engine component delivers high-performance item discovery meeting 99th-percentile response times under 800ms.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons, Librarians, Library Administrators
- Core Services API (Node.js / NestJS)
- Search Engine Container (OpenSearch / Elasticsearch)
- Query Parser & Router Component
- Index & Ranking Component
- Ingestion & Synchronization Component
- Suggest & Spellcheck Component
- Search Analytics Collector Component
- Async Message Broker (RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka)
- Centralized SIEM / Monitoring Platform

## Relationships
- Core Services API -> Query Parser & Router: Submits search DSL/queries [HTTP/REST over TCP]
- Async Message Broker -> Ingestion & Synchronization Component: Delivers catalogue updates [AMQP / Kafka Protocol]
- Query Parser & Router -> Search Analytics Collector: Dispatches search query logs [In-Memory Queue]
- Search Analytics Collector -> Async Message Broker: Emits search telemetry [AMQP / Kafka Protocol]
- Search Engine -> Centralized SIEM / Monitoring Platform: Exposes Prometheus metrics and slow-query logs [HTTPS / Prometheus Scrape]

## Technology Stack
- OpenSearch / Elasticsearch: Chosen for high-performance faceted search, relevance tuning, and built-in Suggester API
- RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka: Decouples write spikes and telemetry logging from search latency to protect the 800ms SLA
- Prometheus: Collects cluster health, JVM heap usage, and slow-query logs for operational monitoring
- Persistent NVMe Storage: Deployed across 3 availability zones in the EU region to guarantee data residency and prevent split-brain scenarios

## Rationale
Decomposing the search container into isolated components with asynchronous ingestion and telemetry ensures strict adherence to the 800ms performance SLA. Circuit breakers, resource quotas, and EU-only NVMe storage guarantee system stability, query-cost governance, and regional data compliance.

Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. The system ensures strict EU-only data residency and sub-800ms transaction responsiveness.

## Key Elements
- PostgreSQL 16: Relational database storing transactional library data within the EU.
- PgBouncer: Sidecar connection pooler managing high concurrent connection spikes.
- pg_partman: Extension automating time-series data partitioning for historical logs.
- `secure_pii` Schema: Isolated database schema containing patron personal profiles.
- `postgres_exporter`: Sidecar exporting Prometheus metrics for query latency tracking.
- `pgaudit` Extension: Tool for streaming security and access logs to centralized SIEM.

## Relationships
- Core Services API -> PgBouncer: TCP/IP via PostgreSQL Wire Protocol with TLS 1.3
- PgBouncer -> PostgreSQL 16: Internal connection pooling via TCP/IP
- PostgreSQL 16 -> Centralized SIEM Platform: Log streaming via `pgaudit`

## Technology Stack
- PostgreSQL 16: Chosen for predictable data footprint control and EU data residency compliance.
- PgBouncer: Selected to handle high concurrent connection spikes from the Core Services API.
- pg_partman: Deployed for automated time-series partitioning to prevent index bloat and maintain query performance.
- Vault: Utilized for secret management and mandatory TLS 1.3 certificate injection.

## Rationale
This architecture satisfies strict EU data residency and GDPR privacy-by-design requirements through isolated PII vaults and automated pseudonymization. Furthermore, multi-AZ clustering, connection pooling, and table partitioning guarantee high availability and sub-800ms performance during peak academic periods.

Async Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for academic and public libraries. It uses an event-driven architecture strictly confined to EU infrastructure to meet data residency and performance requirements.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons, Librarians, Library Administrators
- Web Application (React / TypeScript)
- API Gateway (Nginx / Envoy)
- Core Services API (Node.js / NestJS Modular Monolith)
- Search Engine (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch)
- Database (PostgreSQL)
- Async Message Broker (Apache Kafka on Strimzi/Kubernetes)
- External Systems: EU Identity Provider, S3-compatible EU Object Storage, SEPA/Stripe EU API Payment Gateway, External Notification Service, Centralized SIEM / Monitoring Platform, Interlibrary Loan (ILL) Partners

## Relationships
- Web Application -> API Gateway: Routes client requests [HTTPS / REST / WebSocket]
- API Gateway -> Core Services API: Forwards authenticated requests [HTTP / gRPC]
- Core Services API -> Search Engine: Queries catalog items [HTTP / REST]
- Core Services API -> Database: Persists relational data [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / TCP]
- Core Services API -> Async Message Broker: Publishes domain events [TCP / Kafka Protocol]
- Async Message Broker -> Centralized SIEM / Monitoring Platform: Streams metrics and audit logs [OTLP / Prometheus metrics over TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Apache Kafka: Chosen for immutable, append-only log architecture supporting 30-day compliance replay and EU data residency.
- Node.js / NestJS: Modular monolith design ensuring fast transaction processing for circulation workflows.
- PostgreSQL: Reliable relational storage for core library metadata and patron records.
- Elasticsearch / OpenSearch: Delivers sub-800ms 99th-percentile search performance for catalog items.
- Kubernetes / Strimzi: Manages EU-hosted container orchestration and multi-AZ Kafka replication.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a decoupled, event-driven message broker to ensure high responsiveness and zero data-loss resilience across circulation workflows. Hosting all components within an EU cloud region strictly enforces data residency mandates while maintaining enterprise-grade scalability.
